```python
class MatchTier(str, Enum):
    """How the value was found, from strongest evidence to weakest."""

    EXACT = "exact"              # verbatim in the source
    NORMALIZED = "normalized"    # same after whitespace/unicode/case folding
    SEMANTIC = "semantic"        # same number or date, written differently
    FUZZY = "fuzzy"              # close but not identical: OCR noise, typos
    NONE = "none"                # not found

    @property
    def rank(self) -> int:
        return {
            MatchTier.EXACT: 4,
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED: 3,
            MatchTier.SEMANTIC: 2,
            MatchTier.FUZZY: 1,
            MatchTier.NONE: 0,
        }[self]
```

```python
def match_date(
    value: Any,
    source: str,
    *,
    day_first: bool | None = None,
) -> Match:
    """Locate a date, regardless of the format used in the source."""
    target = parse_date(str(value), day_first=day_first)
    if target is None:
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value is not a recognisable date")

    exact_spans = _find_all(source, str(value))
    if exact_spans:
        return Match(MatchTier.EXACT, 1.0, exact_spans[:5])

    spans = [
        Span(start, end, raw)
        for raw, start, end, found in iter_dates(source, day_first=day_first)
        if found == target
    ]
    if spans:
        return Match(
            MatchTier.SEMANTIC, 1.0, spans[:5],
            note="date present, written in a different format",
        )
    return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="no matching date in source")
```

```python
def match_number(
    value: Any,
    source: str,
    *,
    tolerance: Decimal | None = None,
) -> Match:
    """Locate a numeric value, regardless of how it is formatted in the source.

    This is where most naive grounding checks fail: the model returns
    ``4500.0`` and the document says ``$4,500.00``. Comparing parsed values
    rather than strings is the only way to get this right.
    """
    if is_trivial(value):
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value too trivial to verify")

    target = parse_number(str(value))
    if target is None:
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value is not numeric")

    # Verbatim first, so an exact textual match still reports as EXACT.
    raw = str(value)
    exact_spans = _find_all(source, raw)
    if exact_spans:
        return Match(MatchTier.EXACT, 1.0, exact_spans[:5])

    matches: list[Span] = []
    near: tuple[Decimal, Span] | None = None

    for raw_text, start, end, found in iter_numbers(source):
        if found == target or tolerance is not None and abs(found - target) <= tolerance:
            matches.append(Span(start, end, raw_text))
        else:
            delta = abs(found - target)
            if near is None or delta < near[0]:
                near = (delta, Span(start, end, raw_text))

    if matches:
        return Match(
            MatchTier.SEMANTIC, 1.0, matches[:5],
            note="numeric value present, formatted differently",
        )

    note = "no matching number in source"
    if near is not None:
        note = f"nearest number in source is {near[1].text!r}"
    return Match(MatchTier.NONE, 0.0, note=note)
```

```python
def match_text(
    value: str,
    source: str,
    *,
    fuzzy_threshold: float = 0.85,
    window_slack: float = 0.35,
) -> Match:
    """Locate a string value in the source document."""
    if not value or value.strip().casefold() in _TRIVIAL:
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value too trivial to verify")

    # Tier 1: verbatim.
    spans = _find_all(source, value)
    if spans:
        return Match(MatchTier.EXACT, 1.0, spans[:5])

    # Tier 2: same after folding unicode, whitespace and case.
    norm_source = normalize_text(source)
    norm_value = normalize_text(value)
    if norm_value and norm_value in norm_source:
        idx = norm_source.find(norm_value)
        start = _map_to_original(source, idx)
        end = min(len(source), start + len(value))
        return Match(
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED, 0.95,
            [Span(start, end, source[start:end])],
            note="matched after whitespace/case/unicode normalisation",
        )

    # Tier 2b: punctuation-insensitive. Catches "Acme, Inc." vs "Acme Inc".
    stripped_source = strip_punctuation(norm_source)
    stripped_value = strip_punctuation(norm_value)
    if stripped_value and stripped_value in stripped_source:
        return Match(
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED, 0.9,
            note="matched ignoring punctuation",
        )

    # Tier 4: fuzzy, over a sliding window sized to the value.
    best = _best_fuzzy_window(value, source, norm_value, window_slack)
    if best and best[0] >= fuzzy_threshold:
        score, span = best
        return Match(
            MatchTier.FUZZY, score, [span],
            note=f"closest text in source is {score:.0%} similar",
        )

    return Match(MatchTier.NONE, best[0] if best else 0.0)
```

```python
def parse_date(raw: str, *, day_first: bool | None = None) -> _dt.date | None:
    """Parse a date written in any common human format.

    ``day_first`` disambiguates ``03/04/2026``. Left as ``None`` the ambiguous
    case is only resolved when one reading is impossible (a value above 12),
    and otherwise returns ``None`` rather than guessing, because a silently
    wrong date is worse than an unverified one.
    """
    if raw is None:
        return None
    s = fold_unicode(str(raw)).strip()
    if not s:
        return None

    for pattern, kind in _DATE_PATTERNS:
        m = pattern.search(s)
        if not m:
            continue
        try:
            if kind == "ymd":
                return _dt.date(int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3)))
            if kind == "dmy_or_mdy":
                first, second, year = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3))
                if first > 12 and second <= 12:
                    return _dt.date(year, second, first)
                if second > 12 and first <= 12:
                    return _dt.date(year, first, second)
                if day_first is True:
                    return _dt.date(year, second, first)
                if day_first is False:
                    return _dt.date(year, first, second)
                return None  # genuinely ambiguous; refuse to guess
            if kind == "dmonthy":
                month = _MONTHS.get(m.group(2).lower().rstrip("."))
                if month:
                    return _dt.date(int(m.group(3)), month, int(m.group(1)))
            if kind == "monthdy":
                month = _MONTHS.get(m.group(1).lower().rstrip("."))
                if month:
                    return _dt.date(int(m.group(3)), month, int(m.group(2)))
        except ValueError:
            return None  # e.g. 31 February
    return None
```

```python
def parse_number(raw: str) -> Decimal | None:
    """Parse a human-written number into a Decimal.

    Handles currency symbols, thousands separators in either convention,
    and accounting-style negatives written as ``(1,234.00)``.

    Returns ``None`` rather than raising, because unparseable text is an
    expected input here, not an error.
    """
    if raw is None:
        return None
    s = fold_unicode(str(raw)).strip()
    if not s:
        return None

    negative = False
    # Accounting negatives: (1,234.56)
    if s.startswith("(") and s.endswith(")"):
        negative = True
        s = s[1:-1].strip()

    # Strip currency symbols and codes
    s = re.sub(r"[" + re.escape(_CURRENCY_SYMBOLS) + r"]", "", s)
    s = re.sub(r"\b(?:USD|EUR|GBP|PKR|INR|JPY|AED|SAR|CAD|AUD)\b", "", s, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    s = s.replace(" ", "").replace("\u00a0", "").strip()

    if s.startswith("-"):
        negative = True
        s = s[1:]
    elif s.startswith("+"):
        s = s[1:]

    if not s or not re.search(r"\d", s):
        return None

    # Resolve separator convention by the position of the last separator.
    last_comma = s.rfind(",")
    last_dot = s.rfind(".")

    if last_comma > last_dot:
        # European: dots are thousands, comma is decimal
        s = s.replace(".", "").replace(",", ".")
    elif last_dot > last_comma:
        # US: commas are thousands, dot is decimal
        s = s.replace(",", "")
    else:
        # Only one kind of separator present, or none.
        sep = "," if last_comma >= 0 else ""
        if sep:
            parts = s.split(",")
            # "1,234" -> thousands. "12,34" -> decimal (2-digit tail).
            if len(parts[-1]) == 3 and all(len(p) <= 3 for p in parts):
                s = s.replace(",", "")
            else:
                s = s.replace(",", ".")

    if not re.fullmatch(r"\d*\.?\d*", s) or s in {"", "."}:
        return None

    try:
        value = Decimal(s)
    except InvalidOperation:
        return None
    return -value if negative else value
```

```python
def make_match(tier=MatchTier.EXACT, score=1.0, note="", spans=None):

class TestFieldResult:

def _fr(path, verdict, kind="text"):
    tier = MatchTier.NONE if verdict is Verdict.UNGROUNDED else MatchTier.EXACT
    return FieldResult(path, "v", verdict, make_match(tier), kind)


class TestReport:

    def test_checked_excludes_skipped(self):

    def test_ungrounded_property(self):

        assert [x.path for x in r.weak] == ["a"]

    def test_grounded_property(self):

        assert [x.path for x in r.grounded] == ["a"]

    def test_grounding_rate(self):
        r = Report([
            _fr("a", Verdict.GROUNDED),
            _fr("b", Verdict.SKIPPED),
            _fr("c", Verdict.UNGROUNDED),
            _fr("d", Verdict.GROUNDED),
        ])
        # checked = 3, grounded = 2
        assert r.grounding_rate == pytest.approx(2 / 3)

    def test_grounding_rate_all_skipped(self):
        r = Report([_fr("a", Verdict.SKIPPED), _fr("b", Verdict.SKIPPED)])
        assert r.grounding_rate == 1.0

    def test_get_found(self):
        a = _fr("a.b", Verdict.GROUNDED)
        r = Report([a, _fr("c", Verdict.GROUNDED)])
        assert r.get("a.b") is a

    def test_get_missing(self):
        r = Report([_fr("a", Verdict.GROUNDED)])
        assert r.get("nope") is None

    def test_to_dict(self):
        r = Report([
            _fr("a", Verdict.GROUNDED),
            _fr("b", Verdict.WEAK),
            _fr("c", Verdict.UNGROUNDED),
            _fr("d", Verdict.SKIPPED),
        ])

        assert d["grounding_rate"] == round(1 / 3, 4)
        assert d["fields_checked"] == 3
        assert d["grounded"] == 1
        assert d["weak"] == 1
        assert d["ungrounded"] == 1
        assert len(d["results"]) == 4

    def test_summary(self):
        r = Report([
            _fr("a", Verdict.GROUNDED),
            _fr("b", Verdict.WEAK),
            _fr("c", Verdict.UNGROUNDED),
            _fr("d", Verdict.SKIPPED),
        ])
        s = r.summary()
        assert "1/3 fields grounded" in s
        assert "33%" in s
        assert "1 weak" in s
        assert "1 ungrounded" in s
```

```python
class MatchTier(str, Enum):
    """How the value was found, from strongest evidence to weakest."""

    EXACT = "exact"              # verbatim in the source
    NORMALIZED = "normalized"    # same after whitespace/unicode/case folding
    SEMANTIC = "semantic"        # same number or date, written differently
    FUZZY = "fuzzy"              # close but not identical: OCR noise, typos
    NONE = "none"                # not found

    @property
    def rank(self) -> int:
        return {
            MatchTier.EXACT: 4,
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED: 3,
            MatchTier.SEMANTIC: 2,
            MatchTier.FUZZY: 1,
            MatchTier.NONE: 0,
        }[self]
```

```python
def match_number(
    value: Any,
    source: str,
    *,
    tolerance: Decimal | None = None,
) -> Match:
    """Locate a numeric value, regardless of how it is formatted in the source.

    This is where most naive grounding checks fail: the model returns
    ``4500.0`` and the document says ``$4,500.00``. Comparing parsed values
    rather than strings is the only way to get this right.
    """
    if is_trivial(value):
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value too trivial to verify")

    target = parse_number(str(value))
    if target is None:
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value is not numeric")

    # Verbatim first, so an exact textual match still reports as EXACT.
    raw = str(value)
    exact_spans = _find_all(source, raw)
    if exact_spans:
        return Match(MatchTier.EXACT, 1.0, exact_spans[:5])

    matches: list[Span] = []
    near: tuple[Decimal, Span] | None = None

    for raw_text, start, end, found in iter_numbers(source):
        if found == target or tolerance is not None and abs(found - target) <= tolerance:
            matches.append(Span(start, end, raw_text))
        else:
            delta = abs(found - target)
            if near is None or delta < near[0]:
                near = (delta, Span(start, end, raw_text))

    if matches:
        return Match(
            MatchTier.SEMANTIC, 1.0, matches[:5],
            note="numeric value present, formatted differently",
        )

    note = "no matching number in source"
    if near is not None:
        note = f"nearest number in source is {near[1].text!r}"
    return Match(MatchTier.NONE, 0.0, note=note)
```

```python
def match_text(
    value: str,
    source: str,
    *,
    fuzzy_threshold: float = 0.85,
    window_slack: float = 0.35,
) -> Match:
    """Locate a string value in the source document."""
    if not value or value.strip().casefold() in _TRIVIAL:
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value too trivial to verify")

    # Tier 1: verbatim.
    spans = _find_all(source, value)
    if spans:
        return Match(MatchTier.EXACT, 1.0, spans[:5])

    # Tier 2: same after folding unicode, whitespace and case.
    norm_source = normalize_text(source)
    norm_value = normalize_text(value)
    if norm_value and norm_value in norm_source:
        idx = norm_source.find(norm_value)
        start = _map_to_original(source, idx)
        end = min(len(source), start + len(value))
        return Match(
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED, 0.95,
            [Span(start, end, source[start:end])],
            note="matched after whitespace/case/unicode normalisation",
        )

    # Tier 2b: punctuation-insensitive. Catches "Acme, Inc." vs "Acme Inc".
    stripped_source = strip_punctuation(norm_source)
    stripped_value = strip_punctuation(norm_value)
    if stripped_value and stripped_value in stripped_source:
        return Match(
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED, 0.9,
            note="matched ignoring punctuation",
        )

    # Tier 4: fuzzy, over a sliding window sized to the value.
    best = _best_fuzzy_window(value, source, norm_value, window_slack)
    if best and best[0] >= fuzzy_threshold:
        score, span = best
        return Match(
            MatchTier.FUZZY, score, [span],
            note=f"closest text in source is {score:.0%} similar",
        )

    return Match(MatchTier.NONE, best[0] if best else 0.0)
```

```python
def parse_date(raw: str, *, day_first: bool | None = None) -> _dt.date | None:
    """Parse a date written in any common human format.

    ``day_first`` disambiguates ``03/04/2026``. Left as ``None`` the ambiguous
    case is only resolved when one reading is impossible (a value above 12),
    and otherwise returns ``None`` rather than guessing, because a silently
    wrong date is worse than an unverified one.
    """
    if raw is None:
        return None
    s = fold_unicode(str(raw)).strip()
    if not s:
        return None

    for pattern, kind in _DATE_PATTERNS:
        m = pattern.search(s)
        if not m:
            continue
        try:
            if kind == "ymd":
                return _dt.date(int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3)))
            if kind == "dmy_or_mdy":
                first, second, year = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3))
                if first > 12 and second <= 12:
                    return _dt.date(year, second, first)
                if second > 12 and first <= 12:
                    return _dt.date(year, first, second)
                if day_first is True:
                    return _dt.date(year, second, first)
                if day_first is False:
                    return _dt.date(year, first, second)
                return None  # genuinely ambiguous; refuse to guess
            if kind == "dmonthy":
                month = _MONTHS.get(m.group(2).lower().rstrip("."))
                if month:
                    return _dt.date(int(m.group(3)), month, int(m.group(1)))
            if kind == "monthdy":
                month = _MONTHS.get(m.group(1).lower().rstrip("."))
                if month:
                    return _dt.date(int(m.group(3)), month, int(m.group(2)))
        except ValueError:
            return None  # e.g. 31 February
    return None
```

```python
def parse_number(raw: str) -> Decimal | None:
    """Parse a human-written number into a Decimal.

    Handles currency symbols, thousands separators in either convention,
    and accounting-style negatives written as ``(1,234.00)``.

    Returns ``None`` rather than raising, because unparseable text is an
    expected input here, not an error.
    """
    if raw is None:
        return None
    s = fold_unicode(str(raw)).strip()
    if not s:
        return None

    negative = False
    # Accounting negatives: (1,234.56)
    if s.startswith("(") and s.endswith(")"):
        negative = True
        s = s[1:-1].strip()

    # Strip currency symbols and codes
    s = re.sub(r"[" + re.escape(_CURRENCY_SYMBOLS) + r"]", "", s)
    s = re.sub(r"\b(?:USD|EUR|GBP|PKR|INR|JPY|AED|SAR|CAD|AUD)\b", "", s, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    s = s.replace(" ", "").replace("\u00a0", "").strip()

    if s.startswith("-"):
        negative = True
        s = s[1:]
    elif s.startswith("+"):
        s = s[1:]

    if not s or not re.search(r"\d", s):
        return None

    # Resolve separator convention by the position of the last separator.
    last_comma = s.rfind(",")
    last_dot = s.rfind(".")

    if last_comma > last_dot:
        # European: dots are thousands, comma is decimal
        s = s.replace(".", "").replace(",", ".")
    elif last_dot > last_comma:
        # US: commas are thousands, dot is decimal
        s = s.replace(",", "")
    else:
        # Only one kind of separator present, or none.
        sep = "," if last_comma >= 0 else ""
        if sep:
            parts = s.split(",")
            # "1,234" -> thousands. "12,34" -> decimal (2-digit tail).
            if len(parts[-1]) == 3 and all(len(p) <= 3 for p in parts):
                s = s.replace(",", "")
            else:
                s = s.replace(",", ".")

    if not re.fullmatch(r"\d*\.?\d*", s) or s in {"", "."}:
        return None

    try:
        value = Decimal(s)
    except InvalidOperation:
        return None
    return -value if negative else value
```

```python
class MatchTier(str, Enum):
    """How the value was found, from strongest evidence to weakest."""

    EXACT = "exact"              # verbatim in the source
    NORMALIZED = "normalized"    # same after whitespace/unicode/case folding
    SEMANTIC = "semantic"        # same number or date, written differently
    FUZZY = "fuzzy"              # close but not identical: OCR noise, typos
    NONE = "none"                # not found

    @property
    def rank(self) -> int:
        return {
            MatchTier.EXACT: 4,
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED: 3,
            MatchTier.SEMANTIC: 2,
            MatchTier.FUZZY: 1,
            MatchTier.NONE: 0,
        }[self]
```

```python
def match_number(
    value: Any,
    source: str,
    *,
    tolerance: Decimal | None = None,
) -> Match:
    """Locate a numeric value, regardless of how it is formatted in the source.

    This is where most naive grounding checks fail: the model returns
    ``4500.0`` and the document says ``$4,500.00``. Comparing parsed values
    rather than strings is the only way to get this right.
    """
    if is_trivial(value):
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value too trivial to verify")

    target = parse_number(str(value))
    if target is None:
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value is not numeric")

    # Verbatim first, so an exact textual match still reports as EXACT.
    raw = str(value)
    exact_spans = _find_all(source, raw)
    if exact_spans:
        return Match(MatchTier.EXACT, 1.0, exact_spans[:5])

    matches: list[Span] = []
    near: tuple[Decimal, Span] | None = None

    for raw_text, start, end, found in iter_numbers(source):
        if found == target or tolerance is not None and abs(found - target) <= tolerance:
            matches.append(Span(start, end, raw_text))
        else:
            delta = abs(found - target)
            if near is None or delta < near[0]:
                near = (delta, Span(start, end, raw_text))

    if matches:
        return Match(
            MatchTier.SEMANTIC, 1.0, matches[:5],
            note="numeric value present, formatted differently",
        )

    note = "no matching number in source"
    if near is not None:
        note = f"nearest number in source is {near[1].text!r}"
    return Match(MatchTier.NONE, 0.0, note=note)
```

```python
def match_text(
    value: str,
    source: str,
    *,
    fuzzy_threshold: float = 0.85,
    window_slack: float = 0.35,
) -> Match:
    """Locate a string value in the source document."""
    if not value or value.strip().casefold() in _TRIVIAL:
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value too trivial to verify")

    # Tier 1: verbatim.
    spans = _find_all(source, value)
    if spans:
        return Match(MatchTier.EXACT, 1.0, spans[:5])

    # Tier 2: same after folding unicode, whitespace and case.
    norm_source = normalize_text(source)
    norm_value = normalize_text(value)
    if norm_value and norm_value in norm_source:
        idx = norm_source.find(norm_value)
        start = _map_to_original(source, idx)
        end = min(len(source), start + len(value))
        return Match(
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED, 0.95,
            [Span(start, end, source[start:end])],
            note="matched after whitespace/case/unicode normalisation",
        )

    # Tier 2b: punctuation-insensitive. Catches "Acme, Inc." vs "Acme Inc".
    stripped_source = strip_punctuation(norm_source)
    stripped_value = strip_punctuation(norm_value)
    if stripped_value and stripped_value in stripped_source:
        return Match(
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED, 0.9,
            note="matched ignoring punctuation",
        )

    # Tier 4: fuzzy, over a sliding window sized to the value.
    best = _best_fuzzy_window(value, source, norm_value, window_slack)
    if best and best[0] >= fuzzy_threshold:
        score, span = best
        return Match(
            MatchTier.FUZZY, score, [span],
            note=f"closest text in source is {score:.0%} similar",
        )

    return Match(MatchTier.NONE, best[0] if best else 0.0)
```

```python
def parse_date(raw: str, *, day_first: bool | None = None) -> _dt.date | None:
    """Parse a date written in any common human format.

    ``day_first`` disambiguates ``03/04/2026``. Left as ``None`` the ambiguous
    case is only resolved when one reading is impossible (a value above 12),
    and otherwise returns ``None`` rather than guessing, because a silently
    wrong date is worse than an unverified one.
    """
    if raw is None:
        return None
    s = fold_unicode(str(raw)).strip()
    if not s:
        return None

    for pattern, kind in _DATE_PATTERNS:
        m = pattern.search(s)
        if not m:
            continue
        try:
            if kind == "ymd":
                return _dt.date(int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3)))
            if kind == "dmy_or_mdy":
                first, second, year = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3))
                if first > 12 and second <= 12:
                    return _dt.date(year, second, first)
                if second > 12 and first <= 12:
                    return _dt.date(year, first, second)
                if day_first is True:
                    return _dt.date(year, second, first)
                if day_first is False:
                    return _dt.date(year, first, second)
                return None  # genuinely ambiguous; refuse to guess
            if kind == "dmonthy":
                month = _MONTHS.get(m.group(2).lower().rstrip("."))
                if month:
                    return _dt.date(int(m.group(3)), month, int(m.group(1)))
            if kind == "monthdy":
                month = _MONTHS.get(m.group(1).lower().rstrip("."))
                if month:
                    return _dt.date(int(m.group(3)), month, int(m.group(2)))
        except ValueError:
            return None  # e.g. 31 February
    return None
```

```python
def parse_number(raw: str) -> Decimal | None:
    """Parse a human-written number into a Decimal.

    Handles currency symbols, thousands separators in either convention,
    and accounting-style negatives written as ``(1,234.00)``.

    Returns ``None`` rather than raising, because unparseable text is an
    expected input here, not an error.
    """
    if raw is None:
        return None
    s = fold_unicode(str(raw)).strip()
    if not s:
        return None

    negative = False
    # Accounting negatives: (1,234.56)
    if s.startswith("(") and s.endswith(")"):
        negative = True
        s = s[1:-1].strip()

    # Strip currency symbols and codes
    s = re.sub(r"[" + re.escape(_CURRENCY_SYMBOLS) + r"]", "", s)
    s = re.sub(r"\b(?:USD|EUR|GBP|PKR|INR|JPY|AED|SAR|CAD|AUD)\b", "", s, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    s = s.replace(" ", "").replace("\u00a0", "").strip()

    if s.startswith("-"):
        negative = True
        s = s[1:]
    elif s.startswith("+"):
        s = s[1:]

    if not s or not re.search(r"\d", s):
        return None

    # Resolve separator convention by the position of the last separator.
    last_comma = s.rfind(",")
    last_dot = s.rfind(".")

    if last_comma > last_dot:
        # European: dots are thousands, comma is decimal
        s = s.replace(".", "").replace(",", ".")
    elif last_dot > last_comma:
        # US: commas are thousands, dot is decimal
        s = s.replace(",", "")
    else:
        # Only one kind of separator present, or none.
        sep = "," if last_comma >= 0 else ""
        if sep:
            parts = s.split(",")
            # "1,234" -> thousands. "12,34" -> decimal (2-digit tail).
            if len(parts[-1]) == 3 and all(len(p) <= 3 for p in parts):
                s = s.replace(",", "")
            else:
                s = s.replace(",", ".")

    if not re.fullmatch(r"\d*\.?\d*", s) or s in {"", "."}:
        return None

    try:
        value = Decimal(s)
    except InvalidOperation:
        return None
    return -value if negative else value
```

```python
class MatchTier(str, Enum):
    """How the value was found, from strongest evidence to weakest."""

    EXACT = "exact"              # verbatim in the source
    NORMALIZED = "normalized"    # same after whitespace/unicode/case folding
    SEMANTIC = "semantic"        # same number or date, written differently
    FUZZY = "fuzzy"              # close but not identical: OCR noise, typos
    NONE = "none"                # not found

    @property
    def rank(self) -> int:
        return {
            MatchTier.EXACT: 4,
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED: 3,
            MatchTier.SEMANTIC: 2,
            MatchTier.FUZZY: 1,
            MatchTier.NONE: 0,
        }[self]
```

```python
def match_date(
    value: Any,
    source: str,
    *,
    day_first: bool | None = None,
) -> Match:
    """Locate a date, regardless of the format used in the source."""
    target = parse_date(str(value), day_first=day_first)
    if target is None:
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value is not a recognisable date")

    exact_spans = _find_all(source, str(value))
    if exact_spans:
        return Match(MatchTier.EXACT, 1.0, exact_spans[:5])

    spans = [
        Span(start, end, raw)
        for raw, start, end, found in iter_dates(source, day_first=day_first)
        if found == target
    ]
    if spans:
        return Match(
            MatchTier.SEMANTIC, 1.0, spans[:5],
            note="date present, written in a different format",
        )
    return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="no matching date in source")
```

```python
def match_number(
    value: Any,
    source: str,
    *,
    tolerance: Decimal | None = None,
) -> Match:
    """Locate a numeric value, regardless of how it is formatted in the source.

    This is where most naive grounding checks fail: the model returns
    ``4500.0`` and the document says ``$4,500.00``. Comparing parsed values
    rather than strings is the only way to get this right.
    """
    if is_trivial(value):
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value too trivial to verify")

    target = parse_number(str(value))
    if target is None:
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value is not numeric")

    # Verbatim first, so an exact textual match still reports as EXACT.
    raw = str(value)
    exact_spans = _find_all(source, raw)
    if exact_spans:
        return Match(MatchTier.EXACT, 1.0, exact_spans[:5])

    matches: list[Span] = []
    near: tuple[Decimal, Span] | None = None

    for raw_text, start, end, found in iter_numbers(source):
        if found == target or tolerance is not None and abs(found - target) <= tolerance:
            matches.append(Span(start, end, raw_text))
        else:
            delta = abs(found - target)
            if near is None or delta < near[0]:
                near = (delta, Span(start, end, raw_text))

    if matches:
        return Match(
            MatchTier.SEMANTIC, 1.0, matches[:5],
            note="numeric value present, formatted differently",
        )

    note = "no matching number in source"
    if near is not None:
        note = f"nearest number in source is {near[1].text!r}"
    return Match(MatchTier.NONE, 0.0, note=note)
```

```python
def match_text(
    value: str,
    source: str,
    *,
    fuzzy_threshold: float = 0.85,
    window_slack: float = 0.35,
) -> Match:
    """Locate a string value in the source document."""
    if not value or value.strip().casefold() in _TRIVIAL:
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value too trivial to verify")

    # Tier 1: verbatim.
    spans = _find_all(source, value)
    if spans:
        return Match(MatchTier.EXACT, 1.0, spans[:5])

    # Tier 2: same after folding unicode, whitespace and case.
    norm_source = normalize_text(source)
    norm_value = normalize_text(value)
    if norm_value and norm_value in norm_source:
        idx = norm_source.find(norm_value)
        start = _map_to_original(source, idx)
        end = min(len(source), start + len(value))
        return Match(
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED, 0.95,
            [Span(start, end, source[start:end])],
            note="matched after whitespace/case/unicode normalisation",
        )

    # Tier 2b: punctuation-insensitive. Catches "Acme, Inc." vs "Acme Inc".
    stripped_source = strip_punctuation(norm_source)
    stripped_value = strip_punctuation(norm_value)
    if stripped_value and stripped_value in stripped_source:
        return Match(
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED, 0.9,
            note="matched ignoring punctuation",
        )

    # Tier 4: fuzzy, over a sliding window sized to the value.
    best = _best_fuzzy_window(value, source, norm_value, window_slack)
    if best and best[0] >= fuzzy_threshold:
        score, span = best
        return Match(
            MatchTier.FUZZY, score, [span],
            note=f"closest text in source is {score:.0%} similar",
        )

    return Match(MatchTier.NONE, best[0] if best else 0.0)
```

```python
def parse_date(raw: str, *, day_first: bool | None = None) -> _dt.date | None:
    """Parse a date written in any common human format.

    ``day_first`` disambiguates ``03/04/2026``. Left as ``None`` the ambiguous
    case is only resolved when one reading is impossible (a value above 12),
    and otherwise returns ``None`` rather than guessing, because a silently
    wrong date is worse than an unverified one.
    """
    if raw is None:
        return None
    s = fold_unicode(str(raw)).strip()
    if not s:
        return None

    for pattern, kind in _DATE_PATTERNS:
        m = pattern.search(s)
        if not m:
            continue
        try:
            if kind == "ymd":
                return _dt.date(int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3)))
            if kind == "dmy_or_mdy":
                first, second, year = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3))
                if first > 12 and second <= 12:
                    return _dt.date(year, second, first)
                if second > 12 and first <= 12:
                    return _dt.date(year, first, second)
                if day_first is True:
                    return _dt.date(year, second, first)
                if day_first is False:
                    return _dt.date(year, first, second)
                return None  # genuinely ambiguous; refuse to guess
            if kind == "dmonthy":
                month = _MONTHS.get(m.group(2).lower().rstrip("."))
                if month:
                    return _dt.date(int(m.group(3)), month, int(m.group(1)))
            if kind == "monthdy":
                month = _MONTHS.get(m.group(1).lower().rstrip("."))
                if month:
                    return _dt.date(int(m.group(3)), month, int(m.group(2)))
        except ValueError:
            return None  # e.g. 31 February
    return None
```

```python
def parse_number(raw: str) -> Decimal | None:
    """Parse a human-written number into a Decimal.

    Handles currency symbols, thousands separators in either convention,
    and accounting-style negatives written as ``(1,234.00)``.

    Returns ``None`` rather than raising, because unparseable text is an
    expected input here, not an error.
    """
    if raw is None:
        return None
    s = fold_unicode(str(raw)).strip()
    if not s:
        return None

    negative = False
    # Accounting negatives: (1,234.56)
    if s.startswith("(") and s.endswith(")"):
        negative = True
        s = s[1:-1].strip()

    # Strip currency symbols and codes
    s = re.sub(r"[" + re.escape(_CURRENCY_SYMBOLS) + r"]", "", s)
    s = re.sub(r"\b(?:USD|EUR|GBP|PKR|INR|JPY|AED|SAR|CAD|AUD)\b", "", s, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    s = s.replace(" ", "").replace("\u00a0", "").strip()

    if s.startswith("-"):
        negative = True
        s = s[1:]
    elif s.startswith("+"):
        s = s[1:]

    if not s or not re.search(r"\d", s):
        return None

    # Resolve separator convention by the position of the last separator.
    last_comma = s.rfind(",")
    last_dot = s.rfind(".")

    if last_comma > last_dot:
        # European: dots are thousands, comma is decimal
        s = s.replace(".", "").replace(",", ".")
    elif last_dot > last_comma:
        # US: commas are thousands, dot is decimal
        s = s.replace(",", "")
    else:
        # Only one kind of separator present, or none.
        sep = "," if last_comma >= 0 else ""
        if sep:
            parts = s.split(",")
            # "1,234" -> thousands. "12,34" -> decimal (2-digit tail).
            if len(parts[-1]) == 3 and all(len(p) <= 3 for p in parts):
                s = s.replace(",", "")
            else:
                s = s.replace(",", ".")

    if not re.fullmatch(r"\d*\.?\d*", s) or s in {"", "."}:
        return None

    try:
        value = Decimal(s)
    except InvalidOperation:
        return None
    return -value if negative else value
```

```python
    report = verify({"name": "Alice"}, "Alex was here.", fuzzy_threshold=0.5)

    if fr.match.tier is MatchTier.FUZZY:
        assert fr.verdict is Verdict.WEAK

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    report = verify({"company": "Acme Corp"}, "We work with ACME CORP.")
    fr = report.get("company")
    assert fr.verdict is Verdict.GROUNDED
    assert fr.match.tier is MatchTier.NORMALIZED


def test_verify_whitespace_normalized():
    report = verify({"x": "hello   world"}, "hello world")
    fr = report.get("x")
    assert fr.verdict is Verdict.GROUNDED


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# verify: classifier override
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_verify_custom_classifier():
    calls = []

    def classifier(value, path):

        return "skip"

    report = verify({"a": "Alice"}, "Alice", classifier=classifier)
    assert len(calls) == 1
    assert calls[0] == ("Alice", "a")
    assert report.get("a").verdict is Verdict.SKIPPED

    assert fr.kind == "number"

    assert fr.kind == "text"

    report = verify("Alice", "Alice is here.")
    assert len(report) == 1

def test_verify_trivial_top_level_scalar():
    report = verify("the", "The quick brown fox.")
    assert report.results[0].verdict is Verdict.SKIPPED

# verify: full report properties
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_verify_report_mixed():
    extracted = {
        "name": "Alice",
        "amount": 42,
        "flag": True,
        "missing": "Zebra",

    assert report.get("name").verdict is Verdict.GROUNDED

    report = verify({"amount": 100}, "value 100.5", number_tolerance=Decimal("0.5"))
    assert report.get("amount").verdict is Verdict.GROUNDED
```

```python
class MatchTier(str, Enum):
    """How the value was found, from strongest evidence to weakest."""

    EXACT = "exact"              # verbatim in the source
    NORMALIZED = "normalized"    # same after whitespace/unicode/case folding
    SEMANTIC = "semantic"        # same number or date, written differently
    FUZZY = "fuzzy"              # close but not identical: OCR noise, typos
    NONE = "none"                # not found

    @property
    def rank(self) -> int:
        return {
            MatchTier.EXACT: 4,
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED: 3,
            MatchTier.SEMANTIC: 2,
            MatchTier.FUZZY: 1,
            MatchTier.NONE: 0,
        }[self]
```

```python
    """Locate a date, regardless of the format used in the source."""
    target = parse_date(str(value), day_first=day_first)
    if target is None:
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value is not a recognisable date")

    exact_spans = _find_all(source, str(value))
    if exact_spans:
        return Match(MatchTier.EXACT, 1.0, exact_spans[:5])

    spans = [
        Span(start, end, raw)
        for raw, start, end, found in iter_dates(source, day_first=day_first)
        if found == target
    ]
    if spans:
        return Match(
            MatchTier.SEMANTIC, 1.0, spans[:5],
            note="date present, written in a different format",
        )
    return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="no matching date in source")
```

```python
def match_number(
    value: Any,
    source: str,
    *,
    tolerance: Decimal | None = None,
) -> Match:
    """Locate a numeric value, regardless of how it is formatted in the source.

    This is where most naive grounding checks fail: the model returns
    ``4500.0`` and the document says ``$4,500.00``. Comparing parsed values
    rather than strings is the only way to get this right.
    """
    if is_trivial(value):
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value too trivial to verify")

    target = parse_number(str(value))
    if target is None:
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value is not numeric")

    # Verbatim first, so an exact textual match still reports as EXACT.
    raw = str(value)
    exact_spans = _find_all(source, raw)
    if exact_spans:
        return Match(MatchTier.EXACT, 1.0, exact_spans[:5])

    matches: list[Span] = []
    near: tuple[Decimal, Span] | None = None

    for raw_text, start, end, found in iter_numbers(source):
        if found == target or tolerance is not None and abs(found - target) <= tolerance:
            matches.append(Span(start, end, raw_text))
        else:
            delta = abs(found - target)
            if near is None or delta < near[0]:
                near = (delta, Span(start, end, raw_text))

    if matches:
        return Match(
            MatchTier.SEMANTIC, 1.0, matches[:5],
            note="numeric value present, formatted differently",
        )

    note = "no matching number in source"
    if near is not None:
        note = f"nearest number in source is {near[1].text!r}"
    return Match(MatchTier.NONE, 0.0, note=note)
```

```python
def match_text(
    value: str,
    source: str,
    *,
    fuzzy_threshold: float = 0.85,
    window_slack: float = 0.35,
) -> Match:
    """Locate a string value in the source document."""
    if not value or value.strip().casefold() in _TRIVIAL:
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value too trivial to verify")

    # Tier 1: verbatim.
    spans = _find_all(source, value)
    if spans:
        return Match(MatchTier.EXACT, 1.0, spans[:5])

    # Tier 2: same after folding unicode, whitespace and case.
    norm_source = normalize_text(source)
    norm_value = normalize_text(value)
    if norm_value and norm_value in norm_source:
        idx = norm_source.find(norm_value)
        start = _map_to_original(source, idx)
        end = min(len(source), start + len(value))
        return Match(
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED, 0.95,
            [Span(start, end, source[start:end])],
            note="matched after whitespace/case/unicode normalisation",
        )

    # Tier 2b: punctuation-insensitive. Catches "Acme, Inc." vs "Acme Inc".
    stripped_source = strip_punctuation(norm_source)
    stripped_value = strip_punctuation(norm_value)
    if stripped_value and stripped_value in stripped_source:
        return Match(
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED, 0.9,
            note="matched ignoring punctuation",
        )

    # Tier 4: fuzzy, over a sliding window sized to the value.
    best = _best_fuzzy_window(value, source, norm_value, window_slack)
    if best and best[0] >= fuzzy_threshold:
        score, span = best
        return Match(
            MatchTier.FUZZY, score, [span],
            note=f"closest text in source is {score:.0%} similar",
        )

    return Match(MatchTier.NONE, best[0] if best else 0.0)
```

```python
def parse_date(raw: str, *, day_first: bool | None = None) -> _dt.date | None:
    """Parse a date written in any common human format.

    ``day_first`` disambiguates ``03/04/2026``. Left as ``None`` the ambiguous
    case is only resolved when one reading is impossible (a value above 12),
    and otherwise returns ``None`` rather than guessing, because a silently
    wrong date is worse than an unverified one.
    """
    if raw is None:
        return None
    s = fold_unicode(str(raw)).strip()
    if not s:
        return None

    for pattern, kind in _DATE_PATTERNS:
        m = pattern.search(s)
        if not m:
            continue
        try:
            if kind == "ymd":
                return _dt.date(int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3)))
            if kind == "dmy_or_mdy":
                first, second, year = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3))
                if first > 12 and second <= 12:
                    return _dt.date(year, second, first)
                if second > 12 and first <= 12:
                    return _dt.date(year, first, second)
                if day_first is True:
                    return _dt.date(year, second, first)
                if day_first is False:
                    return _dt.date(year, first, second)
                return None  # genuinely ambiguous; refuse to guess
            if kind == "dmonthy":
                month = _MONTHS.get(m.group(2).lower().rstrip("."))
                if month:
                    return _dt.date(int(m.group(3)), month, int(m.group(1)))
            if kind == "monthdy":
                month = _MONTHS.get(m.group(1).lower().rstrip("."))
                if month:
                    return _dt.date(int(m.group(3)), month, int(m.group(2)))
        except ValueError:
            return None  # e.g. 31 February
    return None
```

```python
def parse_number(raw: str) -> Decimal | None:
    """Parse a human-written number into a Decimal.

    Handles currency symbols, thousands separators in either convention,
    and accounting-style negatives written as ``(1,234.00)``.

    Returns ``None`` rather than raising, because unparseable text is an
    expected input here, not an error.
    """
    if raw is None:
        return None
    s = fold_unicode(str(raw)).strip()
    if not s:
        return None

    negative = False
    # Accounting negatives: (1,234.56)
    if s.startswith("(") and s.endswith(")"):
        negative = True
        s = s[1:-1].strip()

    # Strip currency symbols and codes
    s = re.sub(r"[" + re.escape(_CURRENCY_SYMBOLS) + r"]", "", s)
    s = re.sub(r"\b(?:USD|EUR|GBP|PKR|INR|JPY|AED|SAR|CAD|AUD)\b", "", s, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    s = s.replace(" ", "").replace("\u00a0", "").strip()

    if s.startswith("-"):
        negative = True
        s = s[1:]
    elif s.startswith("+"):
        s = s[1:]

    if not s or not re.search(r"\d", s):
        return None

    # Resolve separator convention by the position of the last separator.
    last_comma = s.rfind(",")
    last_dot = s.rfind(".")

    if last_comma > last_dot:
        # European: dots are thousands, comma is decimal
        s = s.replace(".", "").replace(",", ".")
    elif last_dot > last_comma:
        # US: commas are thousands, dot is decimal
        s = s.replace(",", "")
    else:
        # Only one kind of separator present, or none.
        sep = "," if last_comma >= 0 else ""
        if sep:
            parts = s.split(",")
            # "1,234" -> thousands. "12,34" -> decimal (2-digit tail).
            if len(parts[-1]) == 3 and all(len(p) <= 3 for p in parts):
                s = s.replace(",", "")
            else:
                s = s.replace(",", ".")

    if not re.fullmatch(r"\d*\.?\d*", s) or s in {"", "."}:
        return None

    try:
        value = Decimal(s)
    except InvalidOperation:
        return None
    return -value if negative else value
```

```python
        assert len(r.results) == 1
        assert r.results[0].path == "broken"

    def test_top_level_list(self):
        r = verify(["alpha", "beta"], "alpha beta")
        assert [x.path for x in r.results] == ["[0]", "[1]"]

    def test_top_level_scalar(self):
        r = verify("hello", "say hello")
        assert len(r.results) == 1
        assert r.results[0].path == ""
        assert r.results[0].verdict is Verdict.GROUNDED


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# verify: ignore & classifier
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TestVerifyIgnoreAndClassifier:
    def test_ignore_paths(self):
        r = verify(
            {"name": "hello", "computed": "xyz"},
            "hello",
            ignore={"computed"},
        )
        paths = [x.path for x in r.results]
        assert paths == ["name"]

    def test_ignore_iterable(self):
        r = verify(
            {"a": "alpha", "b": "beta"},
            "alpha beta",
            ignore=["a"],
        )
        assert [x.path for x in r.results] == ["b"]

    def test_custom_classifier_forces_text(self):
        calls = []

        def classifier(value, path):
            calls.append((value, path))
            return "text"

        r = verify({"amount": 4500}, "4500", classifier=classifier)
        assert calls == [(4500, "amount")]
        res = r.results[0]
        assert res.kind == "text"
        # text matching against "4500" -> exact
        assert res.match.tier is MatchTier.EXACT
        assert res.verdict is Verdict.GROUNDED

    def test_custom_classifier_skip(self):
        r = verify({"x": "hello"}, "hello", classifier=lambda v, p: "skip")
        assert r.results[0].verdict is Verdict.SKIPPED


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# verify: integration & report aggregate
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TestVerifyIntegration:
    def test_mixed_report(self):
        extracted = {
            "vendor": "Acme Corp",
            "amount": 4500.0,
            "invoice_date": "2026-01-05",
            "note": "fabricated value that is nowhere",
        }
        source = "Acme Corp billed $4,500.00 on 5 January 2026."
        r = verify(extracted, source)
        by_path = {res.path: res for res in r.results}
        assert by_path["vendor"].verdict is Verdict.GROUNDED
        assert by_path["amount"].verdict is Verdict.GROUNDED
        assert by_path["invoice_date"].verdict is Verdict.GROUNDED
        assert by_path["note"].verdict is Verdict.UNGROUNDED
        assert r.has_hallucinations is True
        assert len(r.ungrounded) == 1
        assert r.grounding_rate == pytest.approx(3 / 4)
        assert r.get("amount") is by_path["amount"]

    def test_skipped_not_counted_in_rate(self):
        extracted = {"flag": True, "name": "Acme"}
        r = verify(extracted, "Acme")
        assert len(r.results) == 2
        assert len(r.checked) == 1
        assert r.grounding_rate == 1.0
        d = r.to_dict()
        assert d["fields_checked"] == 1
        assert d["grounded"] == 1
```

```python
class MatchTier(str, Enum):
    """How the value was found, from strongest evidence to weakest."""

    EXACT = "exact"              # verbatim in the source
    NORMALIZED = "normalized"    # same after whitespace/unicode/case folding
    SEMANTIC = "semantic"        # same number or date, written differently
    FUZZY = "fuzzy"              # close but not identical: OCR noise, typos
    NONE = "none"                # not found

    @property
    def rank(self) -> int:
        return {
            MatchTier.EXACT: 4,
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED: 3,
            MatchTier.SEMANTIC: 2,
            MatchTier.FUZZY: 1,
            MatchTier.NONE: 0,
        }[self]
```

```python
    *,
    day_first: bool | None = None,
```

```python
def match_number(
    value: Any,
    source: str,
    *,
    tolerance: Decimal | None = None,
) -> Match:
    """Locate a numeric value, regardless of how it is formatted in the source.

    This is where most naive grounding checks fail: the model returns
    ``4500.0`` and the document says ``$4,500.00``. Comparing parsed values
    rather than strings is the only way to get this right.
    """
    if is_trivial(value):
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value too trivial to verify")

    target = parse_number(str(value))
    if target is None:
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value is not numeric")

    # Verbatim first, so an exact textual match still reports as EXACT.
    raw = str(value)
    exact_spans = _find_all(source, raw)
    if exact_spans:
        return Match(MatchTier.EXACT, 1.0, exact_spans[:5])

    matches: list[Span] = []
    near: tuple[Decimal, Span] | None = None

    for raw_text, start, end, found in iter_numbers(source):
        if found == target or tolerance is not None and abs(found - target) <= tolerance:
            matches.append(Span(start, end, raw_text))
        else:
            delta = abs(found - target)
            if near is None or delta < near[0]:
                near = (delta, Span(start, end, raw_text))

    if matches:
        return Match(
            MatchTier.SEMANTIC, 1.0, matches[:5],
            note="numeric value present, formatted differently",
        )

    note = "no matching number in source"
    if near is not None:
        note = f"nearest number in source is {near[1].text!r}"
    return Match(MatchTier.NONE, 0.0, note=note)
```

```python
def match_text(
    value: str,
    source: str,
    *,
    fuzzy_threshold: float = 0.85,
    window_slack: float = 0.35,
) -> Match:
    """Locate a string value in the source document."""
    if not value or value.strip().casefold() in _TRIVIAL:
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value too trivial to verify")

    # Tier 1: verbatim.
    spans = _find_all(source, value)
    if spans:
        return Match(MatchTier.EXACT, 1.0, spans[:5])

    # Tier 2: same after folding unicode, whitespace and case.
    norm_source = normalize_text(source)
    norm_value = normalize_text(value)
    if norm_value and norm_value in norm_source:
        idx = norm_source.find(norm_value)
        start = _map_to_original(source, idx)
        end = min(len(source), start + len(value))
        return Match(
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED, 0.95,
            [Span(start, end, source[start:end])],
            note="matched after whitespace/case/unicode normalisation",
        )

    # Tier 2b: punctuation-insensitive. Catches "Acme, Inc." vs "Acme Inc".
    stripped_source = strip_punctuation(norm_source)
    stripped_value = strip_punctuation(norm_value)
    if stripped_value and stripped_value in stripped_source:
        return Match(
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED, 0.9,
            note="matched ignoring punctuation",
        )

    # Tier 4: fuzzy, over a sliding window sized to the value.
    best = _best_fuzzy_window(value, source, norm_value, window_slack)
    if best and best[0] >= fuzzy_threshold:
        score, span = best
        return Match(
            MatchTier.FUZZY, score, [span],
            note=f"closest text in source is {score:.0%} similar",
        )

    return Match(MatchTier.NONE, best[0] if best else 0.0)
```

```python
def parse_date(raw: str, *, day_first: bool | None = None) -> _dt.date | None:
    """Parse a date written in any common human format.

    ``day_first`` disambiguates ``03/04/2026``. Left as ``None`` the ambiguous
    case is only resolved when one reading is impossible (a value above 12),
    and otherwise returns ``None`` rather than guessing, because a silently
    wrong date is worse than an unverified one.
    """
    if raw is None:
        return None
    s = fold_unicode(str(raw)).strip()
    if not s:
        return None

    for pattern, kind in _DATE_PATTERNS:
        m = pattern.search(s)
        if not m:
            continue
        try:
            if kind == "ymd":
                return _dt.date(int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3)))
            if kind == "dmy_or_mdy":
                first, second, year = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3))
                if first > 12 and second <= 12:
                    return _dt.date(year, second, first)
                if second > 12 and first <= 12:
                    return _dt.date(year, first, second)
                if day_first is True:
                    return _dt.date(year, second, first)
                if day_first is False:
                    return _dt.date(year, first, second)
                return None  # genuinely ambiguous; refuse to guess
            if kind == "dmonthy":
                month = _MONTHS.get(m.group(2).lower().rstrip("."))
                if month:
                    return _dt.date(int(m.group(3)), month, int(m.group(1)))
            if kind == "monthdy":
                month = _MONTHS.get(m.group(1).lower().rstrip("."))
                if month:
                    return _dt.date(int(m.group(3)), month, int(m.group(2)))
        except ValueError:
            return None  # e.g. 31 February
    return None
```

```python
def parse_number(raw: str) -> Decimal | None:
    """Parse a human-written number into a Decimal.

    Handles currency symbols, thousands separators in either convention,
    and accounting-style negatives written as ``(1,234.00)``.

    Returns ``None`` rather than raising, because unparseable text is an
    expected input here, not an error.
    """
    if raw is None:
        return None
    s = fold_unicode(str(raw)).strip()
    if not s:
        return None

    negative = False
    # Accounting negatives: (1,234.56)
    if s.startswith("(") and s.endswith(")"):
        negative = True
        s = s[1:-1].strip()

    # Strip currency symbols and codes
    s = re.sub(r"[" + re.escape(_CURRENCY_SYMBOLS) + r"]", "", s)
    s = re.sub(r"\b(?:USD|EUR|GBP|PKR|INR|JPY|AED|SAR|CAD|AUD)\b", "", s, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    s = s.replace(" ", "").replace("\u00a0", "").strip()

    if s.startswith("-"):
        negative = True
        s = s[1:]
    elif s.startswith("+"):
        s = s[1:]

    if not s or not re.search(r"\d", s):
        return None

    # Resolve separator convention by the position of the last separator.
    last_comma = s.rfind(",")
    last_dot = s.rfind(".")

    if last_comma > last_dot:
        # European: dots are thousands, comma is decimal
        s = s.replace(".", "").replace(",", ".")
    elif last_dot > last_comma:
        # US: commas are thousands, dot is decimal
        s = s.replace(",", "")
    else:
        # Only one kind of separator present, or none.
        sep = "," if last_comma >= 0 else ""
        if sep:
            parts = s.split(",")
            # "1,234" -> thousands. "12,34" -> decimal (2-digit tail).
            if len(parts[-1]) == 3 and all(len(p) <= 3 for p in parts):
                s = s.replace(",", "")
            else:
                s = s.replace(",", ".")

    if not re.fullmatch(r"\d*\.?\d*", s) or s in {"", "."}:
        return None

    try:
        value = Decimal(s)
    except InvalidOperation:
        return None
    return -value if negative else value
```

```python
class MatchTier(str, Enum):
```

```python
def match_number(
    value: Any,
    source: str,
    *,
    tolerance: Decimal | None = None,
) -> Match:
    """Locate a numeric value, regardless of how it is formatted in the source.

    This is where most naive grounding checks fail: the model returns
    ``4500.0`` and the document says ``$4,500.00``. Comparing parsed values
    rather than strings is the only way to get this right.
    """
    if is_trivial(value):
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value too trivial to verify")

    target = parse_number(str(value))
    if target is None:
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value is not numeric")

    # Verbatim first, so an exact textual match still reports as EXACT.
    raw = str(value)
    exact_spans = _find_all(source, raw)
    if exact_spans:
        return Match(MatchTier.EXACT, 1.0, exact_spans[:5])

    matches: list[Span] = []
    near: tuple[Decimal, Span] | None = None

    for raw_text, start, end, found in iter_numbers(source):
        if found == target or tolerance is not None and abs(found - target) <= tolerance:
            matches.append(Span(start, end, raw_text))
        else:
            delta = abs(found - target)
            if near is None or delta < near[0]:
                near = (delta, Span(start, end, raw_text))

    if matches:
        return Match(
            MatchTier.SEMANTIC, 1.0, matches[:5],
            note="numeric value present, formatted differently",
        )

    note = "no matching number in source"
    if near is not None:
        note = f"nearest number in source is {near[1].text!r}"
    return Match(MatchTier.NONE, 0.0, note=note)
```

```python
def match_text(
    value: str,
    source: str,
    *,
    fuzzy_threshold: float = 0.85,
    window_slack: float = 0.35,
) -> Match:
    """Locate a string value in the source document."""
    if not value or value.strip().casefold() in _TRIVIAL:
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value too trivial to verify")

    # Tier 1: verbatim.
    spans = _find_all(source, value)
    if spans:
        return Match(MatchTier.EXACT, 1.0, spans[:5])

    # Tier 2: same after folding unicode, whitespace and case.
    norm_source = normalize_text(source)
    norm_value = normalize_text(value)
    if norm_value and norm_value in norm_source:
        idx = norm_source.find(norm_value)
        start = _map_to_original(source, idx)
        end = min(len(source), start + len(value))
        return Match(
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED, 0.95,
            [Span(start, end, source[start:end])],
            note="matched after whitespace/case/unicode normalisation",
        )

    # Tier 2b: punctuation-insensitive. Catches "Acme, Inc." vs "Acme Inc".
    stripped_source = strip_punctuation(norm_source)
    stripped_value = strip_punctuation(norm_value)
    if stripped_value and stripped_value in stripped_source:
        return Match(
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED, 0.9,
            note="matched ignoring punctuation",
        )

    # Tier 4: fuzzy, over a sliding window sized to the value.
    best = _best_fuzzy_window(value, source, norm_value, window_slack)
    if best and best[0] >= fuzzy_threshold:
        score, span = best
        return Match(
            MatchTier.FUZZY, score, [span],
            note=f"closest text in source is {score:.0%} similar",
        )

    return Match(MatchTier.NONE, best[0] if best else 0.0)
```

```python
def parse_date(raw: str, *, day_first: bool | None = None) -> _dt.date | None:
    """Parse a date written in any common human format.

    ``day_first`` disambiguates ``03/04/2026``. Left as ``None`` the ambiguous
    case is only resolved when one reading is impossible (a value above 12),
    and otherwise returns ``None`` rather than guessing, because a silently
    wrong date is worse than an unverified one.
    """
    if raw is None:
        return None
    s = fold_unicode(str(raw)).strip()
    if not s:
        return None

    for pattern, kind in _DATE_PATTERNS:
        m = pattern.search(s)
        if not m:
            continue
        try:
            if kind == "ymd":
                return _dt.date(int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3)))
            if kind == "dmy_or_mdy":
                first, second, year = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3))
                if first > 12 and second <= 12:
                    return _dt.date(year, second, first)
                if second > 12 and first <= 12:
                    return _dt.date(year, first, second)
                if day_first is True:
                    return _dt.date(year, second, first)
                if day_first is False:
                    return _dt.date(year, first, second)
                return None  # genuinely ambiguous; refuse to guess
            if kind == "dmonthy":
                month = _MONTHS.get(m.group(2).lower().rstrip("."))
                if month:
                    return _dt.date(int(m.group(3)), month, int(m.group(1)))
            if kind == "monthdy":
                month = _MONTHS.get(m.group(1).lower().rstrip("."))
                if month:
                    return _dt.date(int(m.group(3)), month, int(m.group(2)))
        except ValueError:
            return None  # e.g. 31 February
    return None
```

```python
def parse_number(raw: str) -> Decimal | None:
    """Parse a human-written number into a Decimal.

    Handles currency symbols, thousands separators in either convention,
    and accounting-style negatives written as ``(1,234.00)``.

    Returns ``None`` rather than raising, because unparseable text is an
    expected input here, not an error.
    """
    if raw is None:
        return None
    s = fold_unicode(str(raw)).strip()
    if not s:
        return None

    negative = False
    # Accounting negatives: (1,234.56)
    if s.startswith("(") and s.endswith(")"):
        negative = True
        s = s[1:-1].strip()

    # Strip currency symbols and codes
    s = re.sub(r"[" + re.escape(_CURRENCY_SYMBOLS) + r"]", "", s)
    s = re.sub(r"\b(?:USD|EUR|GBP|PKR|INR|JPY|AED|SAR|CAD|AUD)\b", "", s, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    s = s.replace(" ", "").replace("\u00a0", "").strip()

    if s.startswith("-"):
        negative = True
        s = s[1:]
    elif s.startswith("+"):
        s = s[1:]

    if not s or not re.search(r"\d", s):
        return None

    # Resolve separator convention by the position of the last separator.
    last_comma = s.rfind(",")
    last_dot = s.rfind(".")

    if last_comma > last_dot:
        # European: dots are thousands, comma is decimal
        s = s.replace(".", "").replace(",", ".")
    elif last_dot > last_comma:
        # US: commas are thousands, dot is decimal
        s = s.replace(",", "")
    else:
        # Only one kind of separator present, or none.
        sep = "," if last_comma >= 0 else ""
        if sep:
            parts = s.split(",")
            # "1,234" -> thousands. "12,34" -> decimal (2-digit tail).
            if len(parts[-1]) == 3 and all(len(p) <= 3 for p in parts):
                s = s.replace(",", "")
            else:
                s = s.replace(",", ".")

    if not re.fullmatch(r"\d*\.?\d*", s) or s in {"", "."}:
        return None

    try:
        value = Decimal(s)
    except InvalidOperation:
        return None
    return -value if negative else value
```

```python
            {"a": "Alice"},
            "the value 99",
            classifier=lambda value, path: "number",
        )
        r = report.get("a")
        # "Alice" isn't numeric -> match_number returns NONE with "value is not numeric"
        assert r.verdict is Verdict.SKIPPED


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# verify — match note handling
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TestMatchNoteHandling:
    def test_trivial_value_skipped(self):
        # "the" is a trivial stopword for match_text
        report = verify({"x": "the"}, "the cat")
        assert report.get("x").verdict is Verdict.SKIPPED

    def test_non_numeric_number_skipped(self):
        # classifier forces number; match_number says "value is not numeric".
        report = verify(
            {"x": "abc"},
            "abc",
            classifier=lambda v, p: "number",
        )
        assert report.get("x").verdict is Verdict.SKIPPED
        assert report.get("x").kind == "number"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# verify — end-to-end
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TestEndToEnd:
    def test_mixed_document(self):
        extracted = {
            "vendor": "Acme Corp",
            "total": 1250.00,
            "invoice_date": "2026-03-15",
            "paid": False,
            "notes": "Net 30 terms apply",
            "fake_field": "Totally fabricated text that isn't here",
        }
        source = (
            "Invoice from Acme Corp\n"
            "Total: $1,250.00\n"
            "Date: 15 March 2026\n"
            "Payment not received.\n"
            "Net 30 terms apply.\n"
        )
        report = verify(extracted, source)

        assert report.get("vendor").verdict is Verdict.GROUNDED
        assert report.get("total").verdict is Verdict.GROUNDED
        assert report.get("invoice_date").verdict is Verdict.GROUNDED
        assert report.get("paid").verdict is Verdict.SKIPPED
        assert report.get("notes").verdict is Verdict.GROUNDED
        assert report.get("fake_field").verdict is Verdict.UNGROUNDED

        assert report.has_hallucinations is True
        assert len(report.ungrounded) == 1
        assert len(report.checked) == 5
        assert report.to_dict()["fields_checked"] == 5

    def test_report_to_dict_roundtrip_shape(self):
        report = verify({"name": "Alice"}, "Alice")
        d = report.to_dict()
        assert set(d.keys()) == {
            "grounding_rate",
            "fields_checked",
            "grounded",
            "weak",
            "ungrounded",
            "results",
        }
        assert d["results"][0]["path"] == "name"
```

```python
class MatchTier(str, Enum):
    """How the value was found, from strongest evidence to weakest."""

    EXACT = "exact"              # verbatim in the source
    NORMALIZED = "normalized"    # same after whitespace/unicode/case folding
    SEMANTIC = "semantic"        # same number or date, written differently
    FUZZY = "fuzzy"              # close but not identical: OCR noise, typos
    NONE = "none"                # not found

    @property
    def rank(self) -> int:
        return {
            MatchTier.EXACT: 4,
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED: 3,
            MatchTier.SEMANTIC: 2,
            MatchTier.FUZZY: 1,
            MatchTier.NONE: 0,
        }[self]
```

```python
def match_number(
    value: Any,
    source: str,
    *,
    tolerance: Decimal | None = None,
) -> Match:
    """Locate a numeric value, regardless of how it is formatted in the source.

    This is where most naive grounding checks fail: the model returns
    ``4500.0`` and the document says ``$4,500.00``. Comparing parsed values
    rather than strings is the only way to get this right.
    """
    if is_trivial(value):
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value too trivial to verify")

    target = parse_number(str(value))
    if target is None:
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value is not numeric")

    # Verbatim first, so an exact textual match still reports as EXACT.
    raw = str(value)
    exact_spans = _find_all(source, raw)
    if exact_spans:
        return Match(MatchTier.EXACT, 1.0, exact_spans[:5])

    matches: list[Span] = []
    near: tuple[Decimal, Span] | None = None

    for raw_text, start, end, found in iter_numbers(source):
        if found == target or tolerance is not None and abs(found - target) <= tolerance:
            matches.append(Span(start, end, raw_text))
        else:
            delta = abs(found - target)
            if near is None or delta < near[0]:
                near = (delta, Span(start, end, raw_text))

    if matches:
        return Match(
            MatchTier.SEMANTIC, 1.0, matches[:5],
            note="numeric value present, formatted differently",
        )

    note = "no matching number in source"
    if near is not None:
        note = f"nearest number in source is {near[1].text!r}"
    return Match(MatchTier.NONE, 0.0, note=note)
```

```python
def match_text(
    value: str,
    source: str,
    *,
    fuzzy_threshold: float = 0.85,
    window_slack: float = 0.35,
) -> Match:
    """Locate a string value in the source document."""
    if not value or value.strip().casefold() in _TRIVIAL:
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value too trivial to verify")

    # Tier 1: verbatim.
    spans = _find_all(source, value)
    if spans:
        return Match(MatchTier.EXACT, 1.0, spans[:5])

    # Tier 2: same after folding unicode, whitespace and case.
    norm_source = normalize_text(source)
    norm_value = normalize_text(value)
    if norm_value and norm_value in norm_source:
        idx = norm_source.find(norm_value)
        start = _map_to_original(source, idx)
        end = min(len(source), start + len(value))
        return Match(
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED, 0.95,
            [Span(start, end, source[start:end])],
            note="matched after whitespace/case/unicode normalisation",
        )

    # Tier 2b: punctuation-insensitive. Catches "Acme, Inc." vs "Acme Inc".
    stripped_source = strip_punctuation(norm_source)
    stripped_value = strip_punctuation(norm_value)
    if stripped_value and stripped_value in stripped_source:
        return Match(
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED, 0.9,
            note="matched ignoring punctuation",
        )

    # Tier 4: fuzzy, over a sliding window sized to the value.
    best = _best_fuzzy_window(value, source, norm_value, window_slack)
    if best and best[0] >= fuzzy_threshold:
        score, span = best
        return Match(
            MatchTier.FUZZY, score, [span],
            note=f"closest text in source is {score:.0%} similar",
        )

    return Match(MatchTier.NONE, best[0] if best else 0.0)
```

```python
def parse_date(raw: str, *, day_first: bool | None = None) -> _dt.date | None:
    """Parse a date written in any common human format.

    ``day_first`` disambiguates ``03/04/2026``. Left as ``None`` the ambiguous
    case is only resolved when one reading is impossible (a value above 12),
    and otherwise returns ``None`` rather than guessing, because a silently
    wrong date is worse than an unverified one.
    """
    if raw is None:
        return None
    s = fold_unicode(str(raw)).strip()
    if not s:
        return None

    for pattern, kind in _DATE_PATTERNS:
        m = pattern.search(s)
        if not m:
            continue
        try:
            if kind == "ymd":
                return _dt.date(int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3)))
            if kind == "dmy_or_mdy":
                first, second, year = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3))
                if first > 12 and second <= 12:
                    return _dt.date(year, second, first)
                if second > 12 and first <= 12:
                    return _dt.date(year, first, second)
                if day_first is True:
                    return _dt.date(year, second, first)
                if day_first is False:
                    return _dt.date(year, first, second)
                return None  # genuinely ambiguous; refuse to guess
            if kind == "dmonthy":
                month = _MONTHS.get(m.group(2).lower().rstrip("."))
                if month:
                    return _dt.date(int(m.group(3)), month, int(m.group(1)))
            if kind == "monthdy":
                month = _MONTHS.get(m.group(1).lower().rstrip("."))
                if month:
                    return _dt.date(int(m.group(3)), month, int(m.group(2)))
        except ValueError:
            return None  # e.g. 31 February
    return None
```

```python
def parse_number(raw: str) -> Decimal | None:
    """Parse a human-written number into a Decimal.

    Handles currency symbols, thousands separators in either convention,
    and accounting-style negatives written as ``(1,234.00)``.

    Returns ``None`` rather than raising, because unparseable text is an
    expected input here, not an error.
    """
    if raw is None:
        return None
    s = fold_unicode(str(raw)).strip()
    if not s:
        return None

    negative = False
    # Accounting negatives: (1,234.56)
    if s.startswith("(") and s.endswith(")"):
        negative = True
        s = s[1:-1].strip()

    # Strip currency symbols and codes
    s = re.sub(r"[" + re.escape(_CURRENCY_SYMBOLS) + r"]", "", s)
    s = re.sub(r"\b(?:USD|EUR|GBP|PKR|INR|JPY|AED|SAR|CAD|AUD)\b", "", s, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    s = s.replace(" ", "").replace("\u00a0", "").strip()

    if s.startswith("-"):
        negative = True
        s = s[1:]
    elif s.startswith("+"):
        s = s[1:]

    if not s or not re.search(r"\d", s):
        return None

    # Resolve separator convention by the position of the last separator.
    last_comma = s.rfind(",")
    last_dot = s.rfind(".")

    if last_comma > last_dot:
        # European: dots are thousands, comma is decimal
        s = s.replace(".", "").replace(",", ".")
    elif last_dot > last_comma:
        # US: commas are thousands, dot is decimal
        s = s.replace(",", "")
    else:
        # Only one kind of separator present, or none.
        sep = "," if last_comma >= 0 else ""
        if sep:
            parts = s.split(",")
            # "1,234" -> thousands. "12,34" -> decimal (2-digit tail).
            if len(parts[-1]) == 3 and all(len(p) <= 3 for p in parts):
                s = s.replace(",", "")
            else:
                s = s.replace(",", ".")

    if not re.fullmatch(r"\d*\.?\d*", s) or s in {"", "."}:
        return None

    try:
        value = Decimal(s)
    except InvalidOperation:
        return None
    return -value if negative else value
```
